title: Equation-by-equation derivation map
scope: Every explicit eq: label in the four specified current source files. Source-qualified labels are used because eq:Ag occurs in two documents. No manuscript prose or equation bodies are reproduced.

rows.concept: Conditional expected reproduction and its logarithm
rows.note: The conditional mean is defined before its logarithm; log target requires a positive finite mean.

rows.concept: Normalised reproductive weighting of parental frequencies
rows.note: Derived from conditional expectation; this is a distribution of parental contributions.

rows.concept: Log differences as proportional changes in conditional mean output
rows.note: Both conditional means must be positive and finite.

rows.concept: Noncommutation of averaging and taking logarithms
rows.note: The distinction is general, not a claim of strict inequality in the conditionally constant case; equality and zero-output cases are explained.

rows.concept: Local quadratic expansion of log conditional expected output
rows.note: The local remainder is retained in the derivation; exact quadratic calculations concern the defined quadratic target.

rows.concept: Mean-centred quadratic component
rows.note: Centring subtracts the population mean of the quadratic term.

rows.concept: Variance of the linear component
rows.note: Finite second moments suffice for this identity.

rows.concept: Gaussian variance of the quadratic component
rows.note: Uses Gaussian fourth moments; the non-Gaussian correction is supplied separately.

rows.concept: First-order share of quadratic log-target variance
rows.note: The share is undefined when the total target variance vanishes.

rows.concept: Population affine projection and curvature-adjusted intercept
rows.note: The population fit includes an intercept; it generally differs from the tangent plane.

rows.concept: Regression and squared-correlation interpretations of the share
rows.note: The correlation form requires positive linear variance; the regression form can have a constant fit.

rows.concept: Ratio of nested fit statistics and the complementary fraction
rows.note: Both fits use the same observation model; the complementary fraction follows by subtraction from one.

rows.concept: Linear and quadratic components under proportional covariance scaling
rows.note: Mean, gradient and Hessian are held fixed; the multiplier acts on variance.

rows.concept: Gradient and Hessian in population-standardised coordinates
rows.note: Whitening uses the positive-variance support if covariance is singular.

rows.concept: Exact quadratic reproductive-weight model
rows.note: An exact model assumption, stronger than a local Taylor approximation; integrability is checked separately.

rows.concept: Exact selected-parent mean displacement
rows.note: Requires positive combined precision and the exact Gaussian/log-quadratic model.

rows.concept: Exact covariance under parental reproductive weights
rows.note: This covariance precedes any model of offspring transmission.

rows.concept: Large variance share with a one-half displacement overestimate
rows.note: The named scalar example is evaluated exactly, then rounded for presentation.

rows.concept: Population-scaled stabilising curvature
rows.note: The symmetric scaled matrix is used in integrability and displacement bounds.

rows.concept: Covariance-scaled relative displacement-error bound
rows.note: Requires a nonzero displacement on the varying support; the relative error is undefined when both shifts vanish.

rows.concept: Covariance update under fixed genic baseline and association retention
rows.note: Derived from the explicitly added transmission closure, not from the variance share.

rows.concept: Genic covariance from allele frequencies and fixed allelic effects
rows.note: Fixed effects do not themselves hold allele frequencies or the genic baseline fixed.

rows.concept: Invariant order interval for the covariance map
rows.note: Positive baseline and retention below one give a positive-definite lower endpoint.

rows.concept: Bounds on every positive covariance fixed point
rows.note: The proof establishes matrix existence and bounds, not general uniqueness or convergence.

rows.concept: One-trait or isotropic covariance update
rows.note: The fraction has a continuous extension at zero starting variance.

rows.concept: Unique positive scalar covariance fixed point
rows.note: The displayed root uses positive curvature; zero curvature is treated separately.

rows.concept: Precision accumulation with complete association retention
rows.note: The no-restoration boundary is treated separately, including singular-curvature limits.

rows.concept: Observation model with a constant conditional log gap
rows.note: A conditional mean-zero error and finite residual variance are additional observation assumptions.

rows.concept: Share after substituting shrunken prediction covariance
rows.note: Slope and curvature stay on the true breeding-value scale; this is not the general naive-refitting result.

rows.concept: Raw relative-fitness phenotype regression and quadratic convention
rows.note: A population least-squares projection, not necessarily an exact conditional mean.

rows.concept: Conversion of selected moments into log-quadratic parameters
rows.note: Moment matching becomes recovery of actual derivatives only under exact log-quadraticity.

rows.concept: Phenotype-fitness model with independent Gaussian environment
rows.note: A specified conditional-mean model; phenotype sufficiency and independence are explicit.

rows.concept: Gaussian environmental convolution of the fitness curve
rows.note: Includes the normalising multiplier as well as the change in width.

rows.concept: Inverse-order covariance contraction under stabilising curvature
rows.note: The congruence proof does not require covariance and curvature to commute.

rows.concept: Phenotype-regression normalisation and selected moments
rows.note: Uses centred Gaussian moments and orthogonality to all fitted regressors.

rows.concept: Selected breeding-value mean from phenotype regression
rows.note: Requires joint Gaussianity, the stated cross-covariance and selection mediation.

rows.concept: Selected breeding-value covariance from phenotype regression
rows.note: Retains conditional breeding-value variance and subtracts the selected mean outer product.

rows.concept: Fixed one-trait curve and Gaussian populations
rows.note: The worked calculation uses m and v where the source uses mu and g.

rows.concept: Variance components for the three one-trait populations
rows.note: Substitution into the Gaussian formulas gives all three population cases.

rows.concept: Population-fitted line for the one-trait walkthrough
rows.note: The mean curvature contribution changes the fitted intercept.

rows.concept: Two-trait surface expressed along and across the gradient
rows.note: An orthonormal relabelling first expresses the same fixed surface in these axes.

rows.concept: Full-population components under physical covariance rotation
rows.note: The quadratic component stays constant here because curvature is isotropic; perpendicular variance remains at 90 degrees.

rows.concept: Conditional expected reproductive output
rows.note: A conditional population mean rather than an individual realised count.

rows.concept: Logarithm of conditional expected output
rows.note: The conditional mean must be positive and finite.

rows.concept: Averaging versus logging individual outputs
rows.note: Includes the equality condition and the obstruction from zero counts.

rows.concept: Normalised reproductive weighting of breeding values
rows.note: The resulting distribution concerns contributing parents.

rows.concept: The guide's Gaussian phenotype-fitness example
rows.note: The guide fixes the optimum and width in the general phenotype model.

rows.concept: Conditional mean for the guide's environmental parameters
rows.note: The general environmental integral is evaluated at the guide's settings.

rows.concept: Expansion of the guide's exact quadratic log mean
rows.note: The stated slope and curvature come from the exact averaged function.

rows.concept: Symmetric finite-difference estimate of slope
rows.note: Exact for the worked quadratic; the Taylor expansion explains its approximation for a smooth function.

rows.concept: Symmetric second difference for curvature
rows.note: Exact for the worked quadratic; outside that model it is a finite-difference approximation.

rows.concept: One-trait quadratic approximation
rows.note: The scalar case of the multivariate Taylor derivation, with remainder qualifications.

rows.concept: Integral over environmental deviations in the guide example
rows.note: Uses the environmental density and the conditional phenotype-fitness mean.

rows.concept: Completing the environmental square
rows.note: The complete square is expanded explicitly inside the environmental-average proof.

rows.concept: General Gaussian environmental convolution
rows.note: Both width and normalising multiplier are derived.

rows.concept: Centred Gaussian moments through order four
rows.note: The scalar moments follow by setting all indices equal in the derived identities.

rows.concept: Centred scalar quadratic component
rows.note: The scalar quadratic mean is removed before the variance partition.

rows.concept: Scalar linear variance
rows.note: The one-coordinate case of the general covariance contraction.

rows.concept: Scalar quadratic variance
rows.note: Uses the Gaussian fourth moment rather than only the variance.

rows.concept: Squared correlation between the linear term and full quadratic target
rows.note: Positive linear variance is required for correlation to be defined.

rows.concept: First-order variance share
rows.note: This source-qualified label is separate from the identically named main-text label.

rows.concept: Population affine-regression R-squared equals the share
rows.note: The regression includes the mean-adjusted intercept.

rows.concept: Scalar least-squares slope equals the local slope under Gaussian quadratic conditions
rows.note: Vanishing third moments remove the covariance of the predictor with centred curvature.

rows.concept: Ratio of noisy affine and quadratic fit statistics
rows.note: The same conditional observation model and response variance are used by both fits.

rows.concept: Proportional covariance scaling of the two components
rows.note: A variance multiplier is distinct from a standard-deviation multiplier.

rows.concept: Scalar selected-parent variance and mean shift
rows.note: Requires positive combined precision; no offspring transmission is inferred.

rows.concept: One-dimensional curvature bound on relative displacement error
rows.note: In one varying dimension the spectral and Frobenius bounds coincide.

rows.concept: Scalar fixed-baseline inheritance closure
rows.note: Reproduction's association-retention rule is additional to the selection calculation.

rows.concept: Numerical endpoints of the scalar invariant interval
rows.note: The guide's trajectory starts inside this interval; other starts need not enter it immediately.

rows.concept: Polynomial satisfied by the scalar equilibrium
rows.note: Obtained by multiplying the fixed-point equation by its positive denominator.

rows.concept: Positive scalar equilibrium root
rows.note: Includes the zero-curvature limit and an equivalent numerically stable expression.

rows.concept: Exact distance formula and scalar contraction inequality
rows.note: The complete-space argument then proves uniqueness and convergence.

rows.concept: Scalar precision after repeated updates with full retention
rows.note: The scalar case of the matrix induction; no positive restoration term remains.

rows.concept: Scalar phenotype regression of relative fitness
rows.note: The half-quadratic convention is stated explicitly.

rows.concept: Relative-fitness intercept and its numerical value
rows.note: Population normalisation determines the fitted intercept.

rows.concept: First selected phenotype moment
rows.note: The scalar version of the Gaussian normal-equation derivation.

rows.concept: Second selected phenotype moment
rows.note: This is a second moment, before subtracting the selected mean squared.

rows.concept: Breeding-value mean and variance conditional on phenotype
rows.note: Requires the joint Gaussian and cross-covariance assumptions.

rows.concept: Selected breeding-value moments in one trait
rows.note: The conditional variance is retained during reproductive averaging.

rows.concept: Scalar inversion from selected moments to log-quadratic parameters
rows.note: The matching parameters recover actual derivatives only under exact log-quadraticity.

rows.concept: Share under fixed-coefficient prediction-variance substitution
rows.note: Does not give a universal bias direction when slope and curvature are refitted.

rows.concept: Four-index reduction of quadratic variance to a trace
rows.note: The matrix-product order is preserved throughout the index contraction.

rows.concept: Multivariate linear variance, quadratic variance and orthogonality
rows.note: The proof allows correlated traits and treats singular support separately.

rows.concept: Multivariate selected-parent mean and covariance
rows.note: Positive combined precision is necessary and sufficient for the Gaussian weight to normalise.

rows.concept: Exact selected displacement in covariance-scaled coordinates
rows.note: The symmetric factorisation does not assume commuting original matrices.

rows.concept: Displacement error in covariance-scaled coordinates
rows.note: Follows from the inverse identity, with matrix order retained.

rows.concept: Relative displacement bound and Frobenius upper bound
rows.note: Equality and zero-gradient cases are given separately.

rows.concept: Multitrait genic covariance from loci
rows.note: Fixed allelic effects and a fixed genic baseline are separate assumptions.

rows.concept: Invariance of the covariance order interval
rows.note: The surrounding proof verifies compactness, convexity and continuity for Brouwer's theorem.

rows.concept: Multivariate breeding-value conditioning on phenotype
rows.note: Left and right covariance factors are retained in the correct order.

rows.concept: Derivatives of the logged phenotype-regression polynomial
rows.note: These are local phenotype-polynomial derivatives, not the selected-moment conversion.

rows.concept: Gaussian latent breeding-value population in the estimation example
rows.note: The companion distinguishes the population mean from centred latent deviation.

rows.concept: Repeated noisy trait measurements
rows.note: Independent measurement environments and wholly additive trait variation are stated assumptions.

rows.concept: Conditional Poisson reproductive-count model
rows.note: Reproduction is independent of measurement environments conditional on the latent breeding value.

rows.concept: Quadratic log conditional expected count
rows.note: The intercept specifies output at the mean breeding value, not population mean output.

rows.concept: Generating linear variance in the worked example
rows.note: The numerical value is a substitution using generating parameters.

rows.concept: Generating quadratic variance in the worked example
rows.note: Individual Poisson variation is excluded from this log-mean target.

rows.concept: Generating variance share in the worked example
rows.note: The theoretical generating share is distinct from a fitted finite-data estimate.

rows.concept: Unbiased within-genotype measurement-variance calibration
rows.note: The derivation states the required sample-size and replication conditions.

rows.concept: Unbiased between-genotype variance calibration
rows.note: Negative realised estimates are possible and are not silently truncated by the implementation.

rows.concept: Calibrated prediction reliability and centred conditional mean
rows.note: Known-parameter identities are derived first; the implementation substitutes fitted calibration values.

rows.concept: Normal latent distribution conditional on repeated measurements
rows.note: The plug-in distribution does not integrate uncertainty in calibration parameters.

rows.concept: Poisson likelihood integrated over uncertain breeding value
rows.note: This averages probabilities, not individual log counts; zero counts remain valid observations.

rows.concept: Slope and curvature of the fitted quadratic log mean
rows.note: The fitted quadratic is differentiated directly at the estimated population centre.

rows.concept: Complete even-part variance with a quartic term
rows.note: The derivation retains the quadratic-quartic covariance term.

rows.concept: Full-curve affine R-squared for the quartic generating function
rows.note: This is a different denominator from the local quadratic variance share.

status_legend.definition: A definition, coefficient convention or explicitly stated model assumption; it is not an empirical theorem.
status_legend.proof: An analytical derivation under stated assumptions. A scalar specialisation or immediate algebraic corollary may share its parent proof.
status_legend.calculation: A stated numerical substitution, worked example, direct differentiation or fitted-model calculation. Numerical values are not substituted for proof.

notation_notes: The one-trait visual calculation uses m and v in the companion where S7 uses mu and g.
The estimation chapter distinguishes centred latent X from the population mean; SF3 uses A in its zero-mean generating model and Z for the centred fitted latent value.
Prediction reliability is R_pred in the companion; reproductive count is R_i. This separates the two meanings represented by r and W in SF3.
The inheritance scalar gamma and the phenotype-regression gamma belong to different models; their definitions are retained locally.

unlabelled_display_review.method: Reviewed top-level equation/align/gather/multline and display-bracket blocks without an eq: label; repeated and intermediate displays are grouped by concept below. TeX linebreaks followed by bracketed spacing are excluded.
